newsitem.title: USA: Nike stock leaps on speculation of Buffett interest.
newsitem.headline: Nike stock leaps on speculation of Buffett interest.

text.p: Nike Inc. shares leaped in heavy trading Wednesday on market speculation that Nebraska billionaire investor Warren Buffett favours the athletic footwear company as an investment.
Nike's Class B stock rose $4.25 to $64.25 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was among the most active issues on volume of more than 2.7 million shares.

Buffett, chairman of Berkshire Hathaway Inc., built his fortune largely through passive investments in undervalued companies overlooked by others. His major investments include insurance giant GEICO and the Coca Cola Co.

"Apparently, there is something out there about GEICO owning a big stake. It was probably done (purchased) when everyone panicked," said a trader, referring to Nike's stock decline to a recent low early last month of about $51.25.

More specifically, another trader said, the Berkshire interest in Nike as investment is likely coming from Louis Simpson, president and CEO of GEICO Capital Operations, Buffett's often-rumoured heir apparent.

"I heard that is it is not him (Buffett) buying the stock, since he said at the (Berkshire) annual meeting he did not understand the sneaker business," the trader said, suggesting that Simpson added Nike to the varied Berkshire investment portfolio.
Buffett's office and GEICO declined to comment, while a Nike spokesman was not immediately available to comment.
Berkshire's Class A shares fell $100 to $42,900 and Berkshire's Class B shares slipped $5 to $1,429.
